theorem m23NormalizedKappaCompactness
    (N : NormalizedKappaCompactnessData)
    (P : M23NormalizedKappaCompactnessPredecessors) :
    Nonempty (RedesignNormalizedKappaCompactnessConclusion N) := by
  classical
  have hlocal : M23LocalCurvatureEstimate N.sequence :=
    m23LocalCurvatureEstimate_of_predecessors N.sequence P
  have hcontrol := m23AllTimeCurvatureControl_of_local N.sequence P hlocal
  obtain ⟨H, F, hF, hcomplete, hoperator, hnc, hnormalized, hmono, hpast⟩ :=
    N.sequence.exists_complete_noncollapsed_closed_geometric_limit P hlocal
  have hbounded : ∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧
      ∀ x : H.limitCarrier.carrier, (F.connection 0).scalarCurvature x ≤ B := by
    exact F.exists_terminal_scalar_bound_of_m23_predecessors P N.sequence.kappa_pos
      hcomplete hoperator hmono
      (fun t ht p r hr hcurv => hnc r hr t ht p r hr le_rfl hcurv) H.base
  obtain ⟨B, hB, hbound⟩ := hbounded
  have hpositive : ∃ x : H.limitCarrier.carrier,
      0 < (F.connection 0).scalarCurvature x :=
    ⟨H.base, by rw [hnormalized]; norm_num⟩
  let K := F.ancientKappaSolutionOfTerminalScalarBound P N.sequence.kappa_pos hB
    hcomplete hoperator hnc hpositive (fun t ht x => hpast t 0 ht le_rfl x) hbound
  have hreference : H.limitCarrier.metricComplete (H.limitFlow.metric 0) := by
    have h := hcomplete (-1) (by norm_num)
    rw [hF (-1) (by norm_num)] at h
    simpa only [neg_add_cancel] using h
  obtain ⟨G, hterminal⟩ :=
    N.sequence.exists_interiorConvergence_terminalExtension_of_ancient_limit
      H K rfl hnormalized hF P hcontrol hreference
  exact ⟨{
    convergence := G
    local_curvature_estimate := hlocal
    all_time_curvature_control := hcontrol
    limit_bounded_curvature := m23LimitBoundedCurvature_of_limit G.limit
    terminal_extension := hterminal
  }⟩

tex_content.source:
\begin{theorem}[Normalized compactness]
\label{thm:ancient-compactness}
The sequence has a subsequence converging smoothly on compact spatial
sets and compact time intervals in $(-\infty,0]$ to an ancient
$\kappa$-solution $(N_\infty,h(t),p_\infty)$ with
$R_h(0,p_\infty)=1$.  One carrier, subsequence, and family of
convergence maps are retained through time zero.
For each $r>0$ there is $C(r)>0$, independent of $i$, such that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_i(0,x)&\leq C(r) &&(x\in B_{g_i(0)}(p_i,r)),\\
 A_i(t,x)&\leq C(r) &&(t\leq0,\ x\in B_{g_i(0)}(p_i,r)).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The limit has globally bounded curvature on each slice.
\lean{PoincareMT.m23NormalizedKappaCompactness}
\uses{thm:ancient-universal,thm:surface-ancient}
\source{MT2007}
\dcref{Theorem 9.64, pp. 225 and 229}
\dcref{Lemma 9.65 and Claim 9.66,
pp. 225--227}
\dcref{Kleiner--Lott, corrected 2013, Theorem 46.1,
pp. 2687--2688, and Appendix E, pp. 2848--2849}
\uses{prop:bounded-ancient-zero-volume,lem:ancient-terminal-cylinder,lem:ancient-collar-sides,lem:ancient-antipodal-collar}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof of local curvature control]
If a volume-controlled ball had unbounded normalized scalar curvature, point
selection and rescaling would give a complete bounded nonflat ancient limit
with positive asymptotic volume. The bounded ancient volume theorem rules this
out. Applying the resulting local curvature estimate around each normalized
basepoint gives the radius-dependent bounds.
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Proof of convergence through time zero]
Curvature derivative estimates and local normal coordinates give smooth
compactness on negative-time windows. Uniform metric-jet evolution extends
convergence through time zero using the same subsequence and embeddings.
Completeness, curvature sign, scalar normalization, and the noncollapsing
implication pass to the resulting limit.
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Proof of the global bound]
Suppose a limit slice had unbounded curvature. Select controlled
high-curvature points and a buffered pointed limit. Splitting and surface
roundness make its local geometry cylindrical. Terminal necks, convex
exhaustion, radial coordinates, and the collared-sphere and antipodal
obstructions rule out an escaping sequence of those necks. This gives the
missing global slice bound and makes the retained limit an ancient
$\kappa$-solution.
\end{proof}
